documents.title: Liver appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body:
I called the liver office and they can see me in March. Is that ok or should it be sooner? Still nursing.

Reply (PCP, 1/12): March is fine. Nothing about your hepatitis C is urgent; the visit is mainly to plan timing of treatment. Bring your questions about breastfeeding.

documents.title: Hepatology follow-up
documents.author: hepatology
documents.body:
HEPATOLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 03/16/2021

Ms. Maguire returns about seven months after delivering at 34 weeks. Treatment for her chronic hepatitis C was put on hold in January 2020 when she became pregnant. She is still breastfeeding and would prefer not to take any new medication until she has weaned. She feels well, with no jaundice or itching.

Meds: prenatal vitamin. Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: anicteric, abdomen benign, no stigmata of chronic liver disease.

Assessment: chronic hepatitis C with no significant fibrosis on elastography in 11/2019 (5.8 kPa). Low short-term risk; deferral is reasonable.

Plan: she will call us when she has finished breastfeeding and is not pregnant, and we will resubmit for sofosbuvir-velpatasvir 12 weeks. No alcohol.

Thank you for allowing us to participate in her care.
Hepatology

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PREVENTIVE VISIT

30F. Doing well. Back at work full time since January. Baby is 10 months, thriving; she is down to nursing at bedtime and expects to wean over the summer.

Hep C: saw hepatology in March, plan is to treat after weaning. She'd like to start in the fall. No symptoms.
No substance use. No tobacco, no alcohol. Sleeping better.

Meds: prenatal vitamin daily (still nursing)
Allergies: NKDA

Exam
General: well, NAD
HEENT: sclerae anicteric, TMs clear, oropharynx normal
Neck: no thyromegaly, no LAD
CV: RRR, no m/r/g
Lungs: CTA bilaterally
Breast: deferred, no concerns, done at OB postpartum
Abd: soft, NT, no HSM
Skin: no jaundice, no rash
Ext: no edema
Neuro: grossly normal
Psych: euthymic

A/P
1. Health maintenance: PHQ-2 0. Pap 2018 normal — cotest due 2023. COVID series completed in April. Flu vaccine in the fall.
2. Chronic hep C — CMP and CBC today. Call hepatology once weaned.
3. IVDU history, sustained remission — doing well.

Return 1 year.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Caitlin — your labs look about the same as two years ago. Liver enzymes still mildly up from hepatitis C, with normal bilirubin, albumin and platelets, which tells us the liver is working well. Kidney function and blood count normal. No changes for now.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Seasonal flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM L deltoid. Afebrile, screening negative. No immediate reaction. Pt asked about calling hepatology; reminded her their number is on the portal.

documents.title: Pregnant again
documents.author: patient
documents.body:
Good morning, just wanted to let you know I'm pregnant again. Positive test this morning, last period started Nov 21. I already called my OB and have an appointment in January. I never ended up starting the hep C meds so nothing to stop. Still taking my prenatal.

Reply (PCP, 12/23): Congratulations! Thanks for letting us know. Keep taking the prenatal vitamin and hold off on any hep C treatment; we'll revisit after the baby. Your OB will handle prenatal care, and we're here for anything else.

documents.title: Refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Refill request prenatal vitamin. Currently pregnant, OB following. Refilled 90 days x 3.

documents.title: Medicaid form
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called asking for a copy of her immunization record for a Medicaid renewal packet. Printed and mailed to address on file; also released to portal.

reports.text: Liver normal in size with diffusely increased echogenicity. No focal hepatic lesion. Gallbladder without stones or wall thickening. Common bile duct 3 mm. No intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary dilation. No ascites. Visualized right kidney unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Diffusely increased hepatic echogenicity. No biliary dilation.

documents.title: Obstetric discharge summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — OBSTETRICS
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admission: 07/24/2022   Discharge: 07/30/2022
Admitting diagnosis: pruritus with abnormal liver tests at 35w0d
Principal diagnosis: acute fatty liver of pregnancy
Secondary: chronic hepatitis C; history of PPROM with preterm delivery (2020); hepatitis B non-immune

HPI: 31-year-old G2P0101 sent in from the OB office after two weeks of intense itching, mostly of the palms and soles and worse overnight. No rash, no yellowing, no nausea or vomiting, no change in stools. She had no prior problems this pregnancy.
Exam on arrival: no excoriations or rash. Fundal height appropriate for dates. Fetal heart tones normal.

Initial labs: total bile acids 45 umol/L; ALT 70, AST 68, alkaline phosphatase 120, total bilirubin 1.2.

Course: repeat labs early the next morning showed glucose 58, uric acid 7.9, WBC 14.8, PT 16.2 seconds with INR 1.5. RUQ ultrasound showed a diffusely echogenic liver without biliary dilation. With these findings the diagnosis of acute fatty liver of pregnancy was made. She was transferred to the ICU for monitoring, started on a dextrose infusion, and induced. Uncomplicated vaginal delivery 07/25/2022 at 35w1d; liveborn infant to the nursery. Glucose stabilized within 24 hours of delivery, coagulation studies and transaminases improved daily, and she returned to the postpartum floor on day 2. Itching resolved after delivery.

Tdap given at the OB office 06/06/2022.

Discharge meds: prenatal vitamin daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP within 2 weeks for repeat CMP, CBC and PT/INR; OB postpartum visit at 6 weeks.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Transition call. Discharge summary from OB admission received yesterday (acute fatty liver of pregnancy, delivered 7/25). She is home with the baby, feels tired but OK. Itching is gone. Eating normally. No confusion, no yellow eyes, no bleeding beyond expected lochia. Booked with PCP 8/9 with labs same day.

events.reason: Post-hospital follow-up, acute fatty liver of pregnancy

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Post-discharge visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Subjective
31 y/o, 2 weeks postpartum. Admitted 7/24 at 35 weeks for itching with abnormal LFTs; next morning low sugar, high uric acid, prolonged PT and an echogenic liver on US, diagnosed with acute fatty liver of pregnancy, monitored in ICU, induced and delivered vaginally 7/25. I reviewed the discharge summary in full.
Today: itching completely gone since delivery. Appetite good. No RUQ pain, no confusion, no easy bruising. Lochia light. Formula feeding this time. Baby well.
Meds: prenatal vitamin. NKDA.

Objective
Vitals reviewed. Well appearing, anicteric. Abd soft, nontender, no HSM. No asterixis. Skin without bruising.

Assessment and plan
1. Acute fatty liver of pregnancy, resolved clinically. Repeat CMP, CBC w/ diff, PT/INR today. Expect enzymes back to her usual mild hep C elevation.
2. Chronic hep C. Not breastfeeding this time — good window to treat. She says she wants to "get settled" first and will think about calling hepatology in the fall. Encouraged her not to let it slide.
3. Mood: PHQ-9 4, tired more than down. Knows to reach out.
4. Flu and updated COVID vaccine in October.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news — your blood sugar, clotting test (INR) and blood counts are normal again, and your liver enzymes are back to where they usually run with hepatitis C. Nothing else to repeat for the fatty liver of pregnancy.

documents.title: Obstetrics postpartum visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
POSTPARTUM VISIT — 09/12/2022
Seven weeks after vaginal delivery at 35 weeks complicated by acute fatty liver of pregnancy. Feels well. No pruritus. Mood stable. Exam normal, uterus involuted. Liver tests per PCP 8/9 back to baseline. Routine follow-up. NKDA. Meds: PNV.

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Influenza quadrivalent 0.5 mL IM L deltoid; Pfizer bivalent COVID booster 0.3 mL IM R deltoid. Screening questions negative. Observed 15 min, no reaction.

documents.title: Hep C
documents.author: patient
documents.body:
I know I said I would call the liver doctor this fall. Honestly with two little ones I can't think about it right now. Can we talk about it at my physical?

Reply (PCP, 11/30): Of course. Your liver tests are stable and your scan in 2019 showed no scarring, so waiting a few months is reasonable. We'll talk at your physical in the spring.
